title: a @throws {never} claim covers the call's panic channel, not the provenance of an object the call returns
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary' (Locked): "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case ... Trusted `@throws {never}` metadata opts out." The subject of that sentence is the CALL. Nothing on that page extends the claim to the methods of a value the call hands back, and a `@throws {never}` factory can legitimately return a handle whose methods throw — so returning an executable foreign value out of `.sm` is refused for losing its panic provenance. This is deliberately a case about a question that is OPEN rather than one that is settled: whether the trust claim should reach the returned type is undecided, and the acceptance direction that works today is 09-foreign-calls/a-trusted-binding-filling-a-smithers-owned-buffer-is-accepted. Without that pair, a lane narrowing the rule cannot tell an intended acceptance from a regression.
